title: BIS applied the Foreign Direct Product Rule to a German firm's foreign-produced MEMS and software shipments to Huawei
source_unit: BIS June 17, 2026 settlement announcement with Robert Bosch GmbH
geography: Germany, foreign production sites, United States export-control jurisdiction, China/Huawei, and consumer-sensor supply chains

observations.period: September 16, 2020 through September 26, 2024 shipments; settlement announced June 17, 2026

denominator.unit: Robert Bosch GmbH settlement covering foreign-produced items exported from abroad

foreign_produced_items.value: MEMS sensor products and automotive software subject to the EAR under the Foreign Direct Product Rule

recipient.value: Huawei Technologies Co. and its affiliates on the Entity List

foreign_shipment_value.unit: U.S. dollars; approximate value of items exported from abroad

license_or_authorization.value: BIS reported exports without the required license or other authorization

voluntary_self_disclosure.value: Bosch filed a Voluntary Self-Disclosure and cooperated with the investigation

bis_penalty.unit: U.S. dollars; penalty agreed with BIS

doj_disgorgement.unit: U.S. dollars; approximate actual payment after partial suspension of DOJ disgorgement

bis_penalty_credit.unit: U.S. dollars; approximately suspended from the BIS penalty as credit for disgorgement

consumer_or_production_effect.unit: missing Huawei product use, Bosch production, customer, worker, sensor availability, or downstream consumer endpoint

strategic_effect.unit: missing deterrence, substitution, PRC capability change, partner response, or U.S. leverage

observations.method: BIS official settlement announcement and PDF review. The foreign-produced route, Foreign Direct Product Rule basis, recipient, shipment value and period, self-disclosure, penalty, disgorgement, and credit are coded as separate cross-border enforcement and remediation stages.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not disclose shipment quantities, exact production locations, item-level classifications, Huawei end uses, the number of transactions, later compliance measures, or production/customer effects. The penalty and self-disclosure establish a realized enforcement resolution, not an enforcement rate or deterrence estimate.
observations.subgroup: Robert Bosch GmbH, foreign production and compliance teams, Huawei and affiliates, MEMS and automotive-software customers, BIS, DOJ, and German/U.S. authorities
observations.counterinterpretation: Foreign Direct Product Rule enforcement can extend U.S. jurisdiction across an allied firm's overseas supply chain while creating compliance and commercial costs; voluntary disclosure may reflect detection and cooperation rather than prior prevention, and the case does not show a change in Huawei capability or broader allied behavior.

related_sources.claim: BIS PDF version of the Bosch settlement announcement.

boundary: This record adds a foreign-produced-item enforcement route: allied firm overseas shipment -> Foreign Direct Product Rule jurisdiction -> voluntary self-disclosure -> BIS penalty and DOJ disgorgement credit. It does not establish later compliance, production or consumer effects, Chinese substitution, deterrence, or geopolitical leverage.
